newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa sees major savings in UAP merger.
newsitem.headline: Axa sees major savings in UAP merger.

text.p: French insurer Axa/UAP expects big savings in the next few years from the merger of the two companies, including around 200 million francs in 1997, the chairman of UAP/Axa France, Claude Tendil, said on Friday.
"We expect 200 million francs of saving in 1997," Tendil told a news conference. He declined to estimate potential savings for 1998, the first year when the real effects of the merger should be felt.
The first "harmonisation" phase will run until 2000 and will bring together their operations, particularly legal, technical, commercial and employment practices.
On the legal front, the company will reduce the number of companies in France from the current 16, which include 13 from Axa and three from UAP.
"It's a bit much, we have to reorganise the group with fewer companies," he said.
Between 2000-2010 the group may reconsider the current decentralised sales network which Axa has been using since 1986.

The group stands to make recurring savings of between 300-500 million francs a year on re-insurance premiums it pays. "It does not seem unreasonable to expect a saving of 300 to 500 million francs a year," he said.
Axa presently pays out 800 million francs in re-insurance premiums and two billion for UAP.
